answers.question: Does your company lend its charging pads to other companies?
answers.expect: no — pads are never lent to another company (3.b2)
answers.answer: My company never lends its charging pads to another company. We have a few dozen charging pads at our own sites, but they are exclusively for our own use.

answers.question: Do the companies want the service to bill their work?
answers.expect: no — the companies do billing and pricing in their own systems (8.b11)
answers.answer: I don't know.

answers.question: Who issues your staff account for the service?
answers.expect: the platform company, outside the service (8.b6)
answers.answer: Staff accounts are issued by the platform company outside the service. I don't know who does it within that company, as I only know my own job as a fleet technician at my operating company.

answers.question: What happens to your drones' reports when radio coverage is patchy?
answers.expect: they come through relay stations and can arrive late, out of order, more than once, or not at all (6.b2)
answers.answer: When radio coverage is patchy, reports from our drones come through relay stations. They can arrive late, out of order, more than once, or not at all.

answers.question: Which sensors can your drones carry?
answers.expect: cameras, thermal cameras, laser scanners — they differ between models (3.b1)
answers.answer: Our drones can carry cameras, thermal cameras, and laser scanners, depending on the model. Different manufacturers make our drones, and they vary in what they can carry, how far they can fly on a full battery, and which charging connectors they use.

answers.question: How long does a drone's battery last on a full charge?
answers.expect: does not know (no figure in the technician slice)
answers.answer: I don't know.

answers.answer: I don't know.

answers.question: What should the service do when an instruction to a charging pad may have got through twice?
answers.expect: describes the situation and what worries it, proposes no checks, screens, features or mechanisms
answers.answer: I don't know anything about how the service handles that. I just know that the links used to give instructions to the charging equipment are unreliable, and an instruction may get through twice while the sender often cannot tell whether the first attempt arrived.

answers.question: What kinds of jobs do your drones fly?
answers.expect: deliveries, which carry a load from one site to another, and inspections, which visit a list of points in a set order and return (4.b1, 4.b2)
answers.answer: Our drones fly deliveries, which carry a load from one site to another. They also fly inspections, taking a drone with the right sensors to a list of points in a set order and bringing it back to the starting point.

answers.question: Are the companies seeking certification from the platform?
answers.expect: no — none of them is; they expect it to respect how the rules work in practice (5.b3)
answers.answer: None of our companies is seeking certification from the platform. We expect the platform to respect how the EU drone operation rules and EU U-space rules work in practice.

answers.question: Do the companies want management reports or dashboards from the service?
answers.expect: no — not beyond day-to-day operations (8.b1)
answers.answer: We do not want management or analytical reports, exports, and dashboards beyond day-to-day operations.

answers.question: Should you be able to log in with your company's corporate identity system?
answers.expect: no — the companies do not want logging in through their own identity systems (8.b2)
answers.answer: We do not want to log in through our own corporate identity systems. Staff accounts are issued by the platform company outside the service instead.
